## 1 Abstract

DiallelAnalysisR analyses diallel crosses laid out in randomized
complete blocks. This vignette takes one data set, an eight-parent
diallel with reciprocals, from the plot data to the analysis of
variance, the combining-ability effects with their standard errors and
the plots, in a few minutes of reading. Each later vignette takes one
part further.

## 2 The data

Each row is one plot: the female parent (`Cross1`), the male parent
(`Cross2`), the replicate (`Rep`) and the yield.

``` r

head(GriffingData1)
```

      Cross1 Cross2 Rep  Yield
    1      1      1   1 104.86
    2      1      2   1  88.66
    3      1      3   1 109.76
    4      1      4   1 128.10
    5      1      5   1 128.36
    6      1      6   1  74.40

``` r

dim(GriffingData1)
```

    [1] 256   4

``` r

with(data = GriffingData1, expr = table(Cross1, Cross2))[1:4, 1:4]
```

          Cross2
    Cross1 1 2 3 4
         1 4 4 4 4
         2 4 4 4 4
         3 4 4 4 4
         4 4 4 4 4

The 8 parents, their 28 crosses and the 28 reciprocal crosses (64 cells)
are each grown in 4 replicates.

## 3 One analysis

Griffing’s Method 1 (parents, \\F_1\\ and reciprocals) with the
fixed-effects model (Model 1):

``` r

fit <-
  Griffing(
      y          = Yield
    , Rep        = Rep
    , Cross1     = Cross1
    , Cross2     = Cross2
    , data       = GriffingData1
    , Method     = 1
    , Model      = 1
    , Reciprocal = c("combined", "split")[1]
    )
fit
```

## 4 The analysis of variance

``` r

knitr::kable(x = fit$ANOVA, digits = 3)
```

|             |  Df |    Sum Sq | Mean Sq | F value | Pr(\>F) |
|:------------|----:|----------:|--------:|--------:|--------:|
| gca         |   7 |  3804.643 | 543.520 |  18.887 |   0.000 |
| sca         |  28 | 22060.789 | 787.885 |  27.378 |   0.000 |
| reciprocals |  28 |   365.537 |  13.055 |   0.454 |   0.992 |
| Error       | 189 |  5438.991 |  28.778 |      NA |      NA |

General and specific combining ability are both highly significant; the
reciprocal differences are not. The mean squares are on the scale of a
cell mean, so the error line is \\MS_E/B\\, the residual mean square of
the block analysis divided by the number of replicates.

## 5 Effects and standard errors

``` r

round(x = fit$GCA, digits = 3)
```

         1      2      3      4      5      6      7      8
     0.062  0.468  9.027 -3.438 -2.325 -1.935  7.238 -9.096 

``` r

round(x = fit$StdErr, digits = 3)
```

         gi     sii     sij     rij   gi_gj sii_sjj sii_sij sii_sjk sij_sik sij_skl
      1.255   4.694   3.353   3.793   1.897   6.570   6.290   5.690   5.018   4.646
    rij_rkl
      5.364 

Parents 3 and 7 are the best general combiners, parent 8 the poorest. A
difference between two gca effects larger than about twice `gi_gj` is
significant at about the 5% level.

## 7 The usual model functions

[`summary()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/summary.html) adds the \\t\\ tests
of every gca effect and the crosses with the largest sca effects;
[`anova()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/anova.html),
[`coef()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/coef.html),
[`vcov()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/vcov.html),
[`confint()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/confint.html),
[`fitted()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/fitted.values.html),
[`residuals()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/residuals.html) and
[`predict()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/predict.html) work as for other
models in R.

``` r

summary(object = fit, top = 5)
```

## 8 Tables for a report

Any component converts to a table, with the row names in a column
`term`:

``` r

data.table::as.data.table(fit, component = "ANOVA")
```

## 9 Summary

One call of
[`Griffing()`](https://myaseen208.com/DiallelAnalysisR/reference/Griffing.md)
gives the analysis of variance, the effects with their standard errors
and the variance components;
[`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) draws the
effects. Vignette 02 helps choose an analysis; vignettes 04 to 07
explain Griffing’s, Hayman’s and the partial diallel analyses, 08 to 11
heterosis, related designs, environments and planning, and 12 the tables
for papers and the interactive application. Vignettes 13 to 15 cover
validation, speed and extending the package.

## 10 References

Griffing, B. (1956). Concept of general and specific combining ability
in relation to diallel crossing systems. *Australian Journal of
Biological Sciences*, 9(4), 463–493.

Singh, R. K. and Chaudhary, B. D. (2004). *Biometrical Methods in
Quantitative Genetic Analysis*. Kalyani Publishers, New Delhi.
